A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InterpretCC and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained architectures and experiments can be matched despite substantial restructuring and additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original predictive experiments on education, text, and healthcare datasets, plus sparsity and routing analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original predictive experiments, synthetic explanation evaluations, and a teacher user study, including additional appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The core discriminator, Gumbel gating, feature masking, and weighted expert aggregation remain unchanged. v2 adds a specific grouping procedure for synthetic data: assigning each feature to the cluster with the greatest mean absolute feature value (Section 4). This is a limited grouping adaptation within the existing architecture.

E1.justification: v2 adds OpenXAI synthetic data with ground-truth explanations and a teacher evaluation, introducing explanation-recovery and human-assessment tasks. The main EDU comparison narrows from six courses to four, but Structures and Ventures remain represented in Appendix G.2.3. AG News, SST, and Breast Cancer remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds NAM and SENN feature/concept baselines to non-text predictive and synthetic explanation comparisons, and compares NAM/SENN explanations in the user study. Top-k routing is newly included in EDU comparisons; its renamed text/health counterpart already existed in v1. The fixed-feature BiLSTM comparison disappears with the earlier DSP ablations.

E3.justification: New protocols include synthetic explanation accuracy and Pairwise Rank Agreement, plus a user study using four randomly selected DSP students, randomized explanation order, and five Likert-scale criteria. Appendix D reports excluding five of 56 recruited participants. Retained EDU splits and prediction horizons are unchanged; newly disclosed tuning grids and epoch budgets do not establish changes to earlier training settings.

E4.justification: v2 removes much of v1 Appendix E: dynamic versus fixed feature selection, easy-hard and pretrained-expert comparisons, unweighted versus weighted routing, threshold sensitivity, and route-behavior diagnostics. The 40%/60% sparsity comparison survives as Table 11, and six-course grouping plots survive in Appendix G. This substantially reduces architectural ablation evidence without deleting all earlier analyses.

E5.justification: v1 labels main results as means with 99% confidence intervals and gives EDU routing point estimates. v2 newly specifies three random seeds, reports means and standard deviations, uses 95% intervals for comparisons, and supplies EDU routing uncertainty. It also adds Friedman, ANOVA, and Tukey HSD analyses. The newly disclosed seed count does not demonstrate an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline, synthetic-faithfulness, and teacher-rating results while removing many DSP appendix results and main Structures/Ventures performance rows. Retained numbers also change: Breast Cancer Feature Gating is 74.67 in v1 versus 78.19 in v2. Group Routing means 94.85, 90.35, and 91.75 belong to AG News, SST, and Breast Cancer in v1 Table 5, but Breast Cancer, AG News, and SST in v2 Table 2. Corresponding top-k values are similarly reassigned without explanation; these cannot establish performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gumbel sampling, sigmoid reduction, and straight-through estimator derivations are retained from v1 Appendix C in v2 Appendix F. Main masking equations use revised masked-input notation without substantive mathematical change. No theorems, proofs, or formal metric derivations are added.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims interpretable architectures with competitive predictive performance. v2 adds headline claims of outperforming interpretable baselines and receiving better human assessments, makes the user study a separate contribution, and incorporates synthetic evaluation into its stated scope. The original sparse, user-defined interpretability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of explanation-presentation confounds, limited user-study generalizability, appropriate uses of each architecture, tuning sensitivity, and validation before production use. Conversely, it removes v1 Appendix E's warning that route weights can reflect majority-class prediction rather than feature importance and depend on initialization. These materially change the qualifications attached to interpretability claims.

D1.justification: New Appendices A, D, and E document dataset statistics, access/licensing and EDU privacy restrictions, survey materials and compensation, hardware and training times, hyperparameter grids, and epoch budgets. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Some earlier details disappear, including the padding instruction and explicit feature-set provenance of the 97-feature DSP case study retained in Table 11.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning through Background and Table 1, contrasting faithfulness, sparsity, coverage, granularity, and user-defined concepts. SENN and NAM become central related methods, with new references supporting synthetic evaluation and study design. Several sources associated with the removed DSP case study disappear. This exceeds citation renumbering or relocation.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the title, introduction, background, and conclusion, moves related work before methodology, and reorganizes results around performance, faithfulness, and human preference. Dataset/grouping explanations move into expanded appendices, the DSP case study is abridged, and a conference checklist is inserted. The narrative structure changes substantially.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Separate architecture diagrams merge into Figure 1; performance tables are consolidated and expanded with color-coded comparisons. v2 adds conceptual and user-study displays, relocates grouping tables and activation figures to appendices, and removes several DSP diagnostic tables and plots. Many retained graphics are redisplayed rather than new results.

improvement.justification: The synthetic evaluation, interpretable baselines, teacher study, and reproducibility details address important gaps in v1. However, v2 removes substantial ablation evidence and a consequential warning about interpreting route weights. Routing score pairs are reassigned across datasets without explanation between v1 Table 5 and v2 Table 2. Section 5.3 also claims significant superiority over SENN on trustworthiness, whereas Figure 11 does not mark that comparison significant. These unresolved issues affect central performance and interpretability evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the substantial additions.
